description: Statutory allergen lists per market: the UK/EU 14 and the US 9. Source of data/ops/market_allergens.json (ops writer adds the __schema__ sentinel). Codes are <market>:<group>, using the extraction groups milk, egg, fish, crustacean, mollusc, tree_nut, peanut, gluten_cereal, wheat, soy, sesame, celery, mustard, lupin, sulphite.

UK.statute: Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011 on the provision of food information to consumers, Annex II (assimilated law in Great Britain since 1 January 2024)
UK.guidance: Food Standards Agency, Allergen guidance for food businesses, section 1 '14 allergens' (GOV.UK, last updated 17 July 2026)
UK.transcribed_from: The FSA guidance page, fetched 2026-10-23. The legislation.gov.uk and EUR-Lex pages answered automated fetches with an anti-bot challenge (HTTP 202, empty body), so Annex II item numbers follow the regulation's numbering and are not machine-verified here.

US.statute: FD&C Act section 201(qq) (21 U.S.C. 321(qq)) as added by FALCPA 2004 (Public Law 108-282) and amended by the FASTER Act 2021 (Public Law 117-11, sesame)
US.guidance: FDA, Questions and Answers Regarding Food Allergens, Including the Food Allergen Labeling Requirements of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (Edition 5): Guidance for Industry, January 2025 (nonbinding)
US.faq: FDA, Frequently Asked Questions: Food Allergen Labeling Guidance for Industry (content current as of 03/26/2025)
US.sesame_effective: The FDA Food Allergies page states the sesame change 'was effective on January 1, 2023' (https://www.fda.gov/food/nutrition-food-labeling-and-critical-foods/food-allergies).
US.transcribed_from: Edition 5 PDF fetched 2026-10-23 (27 pages): A.1 list of major food allergens (p. 4), C.1 milk, C.3 eggs (p. 13), C.7 and Table 1 tree nuts (pp. 14-15), C.8 (pp. 15-16), C.9 wheat and C.11 soy synonyms (p. 16), D.9 highly refined oils (pp. 20-21). FAQ page fetched 2026-10-23 for the coconut answer and the removed-nut list.
US.licence: US federal government work, public domain

rule_conflicts.summary: Coconut is not a tree nut for labelling in either market, but older US labels and FDA recall texts may still call it one.
rule_conflicts.US: FDA FAQ: 'No, coconut is no longer listed in the Tree Nut List (Table 1) in the 5th edition of the Food Allergen Q&A Guidance.' FDA expects 'a transitional period before firms remove coconut from the Contains statement'. Table 1 tree nuts not listed 'should not be included in the Contains statement' but must stay in the ingredient list (Q&A C.8).
rule_conflicts.UK: Annex II item 8 (Nuts) names almonds, hazelnuts, walnuts, cashews, pecans, Brazil nuts, pistachios and macadamia (Queensland) nuts; coconut is not listed.
rule_conflicts.example: openFDA H-1274-2026 / H-1275-2026 (Lidl Eridanous shortbread) give the reason 'undeclared ... tree nut (coconut)'.
rule_conflicts.handling: Surface as a rule-against-rule conflict; never list coconut under 'Contains' for either market; keep it in the ingredient list.

rule_conflicts.summary: Pine nuts are a US Table 1 tree nut but are not an Annex II nut.
rule_conflicts.UK: Annex II item 8 does not list pine nuts.
rule_conflicts.handling: US:tree_nut covers pine nut; UK statements name pine nut only in the ingredient list.

rule_conflicts.summary: The UK declares 'cereals containing gluten' (wheat, rye, barley, oats); the US declares 'wheat' only (any Triticum species).
rule_conflicts.handling: US:gluten_cereal is deliberately absent, so a US-market gluten tag becomes an FK DQ orphan and the US statement must say 'wheat'. Barley, rye and oats are not US major food allergens.

data.statute: FD&C Act 201(qq), 21 U.S.C. 321(qq) (FALCPA 2004, Pub. L. 108-282)

data.notes: Q&A C.1: FDA considers 'milk' as milk from domesticated cows, goats, sheep, or other ruminants; C.2: name the animal for non-cow milk (e.g. 'goat milk').

data.statute: FD&C Act 201(qq), 21 U.S.C. 321(qq) (FALCPA 2004, Pub. L. 108-282)
data.edition: FDA Food Allergen Q&A Edition 5, Jan 2025, Q&A C.9
includes: any species in the genus Triticum: common wheat, durum wheat, club wheat, spelt, semolina, Einkorn, emmer, Khorasan, triticale
data.notes: Q&A C.9 defines wheat as any Triticum species. Gluten is not itself a US major food allergen; the US statement says 'wheat'.

data.notes: Q&A C.11: 'Soybean,' 'soy,' and 'soya' are reasonable synonyms. Q&A D.9: highly refined oils derived from a major food allergen are exempt from section 403(w), but the source still appears in the ingredient list (e.g. 'soybean oil').
